identification.summary: Iranian threat actor that Microsoft tracks as Pink Sandstorm (also known as Agrius) [S2]; public reporting has linked it to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) [S3]. It is known for destructive wiper and fake-ransomware operations focused on Israeli targets since 2020 [S3][S4]. Over time its operations moved from wipers disguised as ransomware (DEADWOOD, Apostle) to supply-chain wiper deployment (Fantasy, 2022), new ransomware (Moneybird, 2023), and data theft followed by wiping in Israeli higher education and technology (2023) [S4][S6][S7][S9]. In December 2023 Israel's National Cyber Directorate named Agrius, working with Hezbollah's Lebanese Cedar, in a late-November 2023 attack on Ziv Medical Center [S10].
identification.firstObserved: SentinelLabs observed Agrius operating in Israel starting in 2020 [S4]. MITRE also dates the group's activity to 2020 [S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Pink Sandstorm (formerly AMERICIUM). Microsoft lists SPECTRAL KITTEN, Agrius, Deadwood, BlackShadow, SharpBoys, FireAnt and Justice Blade as other names [S2]. Palo Alto Unit 42 tracks the group as Agonizing Serpens and equates it with Agrius, BlackShadow, Pink Sandstorm and DEV-0022 [S9]. MITRE tracks it as Agrius (G1030) [S3]. Check Point says the group has operated under multiple aliases and leaked Moneybird victim data through one of its previous personas [S7][S8]. BlackShadow is the persona that extorted Israeli insurer Shirbit in 2020 [S8].

attribution.sponsor: Iran, Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). MITRE notes that public reporting has linked Agrius to MOIS [S3]. Israel's National Cyber Directorate (INCD), as reported by the press, described Agrius as affiliated with the Iranian Ministry of Intelligence [S10].
attribution.confidence: SentinelLabs (2021) assessed with medium confidence that Agrius is of Iranian origin [S4]. Check Point (2023) said the group's affiliation was not fully clear [S8]. The INCD attribution of the Ziv Medical Center attack is an Israeli government statement reported by the press [S10]; no US government attribution was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Vendor incident response and malware analysis (SentinelLabs, ESET, Check Point, Unit 42) [S4][S6][S7][S9]; INCD statement on the Ziv Medical Center incident, based on a joint investigation with the IDF and Shin Bet [S10].

objectives: Disruption and destruction against Israeli organizations, with ransomware used as cover rather than for profit; SentinelLabs judged it unlikely that Agrius is financially motivated [S4]. Espionage and data theft come before destructive operations [S4][S9].

sectors: HR consulting and IT support services [S6]
targeting.notes: Israel is the consistent focus across all vendor reporting [S3][S4][S9]. Victims outside Israel came through the 2022 supply-chain compromise of an Israeli software developer [S6]. Check Point did not specify which sectors Moneybird hit [S8].

capabilities.summary: Initial access usually comes through internet-facing web servers and known vulnerabilities, including FortiOS CVE-2018-13379, and is followed by ASPXSpy web shells [S5][S7]. After access the group uses public tools for lateral movement, credential harvesting and exfiltration [S7]. Its custom destructive tooling has evolved over time: the DEADWOOD wiper; the .NET Apostle wiper, which later gained working ransomware encryption; and the IPsec Helper .NET backdoor [S4]. Fantasy, a wiper built from Apostle code, was pushed through a compromised Israeli software vendor's updates; the campaign lasted under three hours [S6]. Moneybird is C++ ransomware using AES-256 GCM [S7][S8]. In 2023 the group used the MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer wipers and the Sqlextractor database-theft tool. It also switched between public proof-of-concept tools and custom code to evade EDR [S9].

campaigns.name: Shirbit attack (BlackShadow persona)
campaigns.summary: Agrius hit Israeli insurer Shirbit with ransomware in late 2020; BlackShadow was the extortion persona.

campaigns.name: DEADWOOD/Apostle wiper-as-ransomware operations
campaigns.summary: SentinelLabs reports Agrius moving from espionage to destructive attacks on Israeli targets, using DEADWOOD and Apostle wipers disguised as ransomware and the IPsec Helper backdoor.

campaigns.name: Bar-Ilan University wiper attack
campaigns.summary: The Record reports that Agrius hit Bar-Ilan University with wipers in 2021.

campaigns.name: Fantasy wiper supply-chain attack
campaigns.summary: After deploying credential harvesters on 20 Feb 2022, Agrius abused an Israeli diamond-industry software developer to wipe customers in Israel, South Africa and Hong Kong in under three hours.

campaigns.name: Israeli higher education and technology campaign
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 reports data theft followed by MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer wipers to cover tracks and disable systems.

campaigns.name: Moneybird ransomware
campaigns.summary: Check Point attributes new C++ Moneybird ransomware against Israeli organizations to Agrius; victim data was later leaked through a prior Agrius alias.

campaigns.name: Ziv Medical Center attack
campaigns.summary: The INCD said Agrius, working with Hezbollah's Lebanese Cedar, attacked Ziv Medical Center in late November 2023; the attackers claimed to have stolen patient records.

diamond.adversary: MOIS-linked Iranian operators (Pink Sandstorm/Agrius) using rotating personas such as BlackShadow [S3][S8]. The INCD reported Agrius working with Hezbollah's Lebanese Cedar [S10].
diamond.capability: Web-server exploitation and ASPXSpy web shells [S7]. Wipers include DEADWOOD, Apostle, Fantasy, MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer; other tools are Moneybird ransomware, the IPsec Helper backdoor and Sqlextractor [S4][S6][S7][S9].
diamond.infrastructure: A compromised software vendor's update channel [S6]; leak personas and channels used to publish stolen data [S7][S8].
diamond.victim: Israeli insurance, higher education, technology, diamond and healthcare organizations, plus supply-chain victims in South Africa and Hong Kong [S6][S8][S9][S10].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iran-Israel confrontation [S3][S10]. The ransomware disguise provides deniability for state-directed disruption [S4].
diamond.technology: Exposure of internet-facing web applications and VPN appliances (FortiOS) [S5][S7]; trusted software update paths [S6]; Windows enterprise networks and database servers [S9].

gaps: No Microsoft reporting on Pink Sandstorm operations was verified during fact-check; Microsoft detail here is limited to the naming page [S2].
Microsoft alias list includes Justice Blade, SharpBoys and FireAnt, but no cited source describes the operations behind those personas [S2].

Attribution of the Ziv Medical Center incident: the INCD named Agrius with Lebanese Cedar, while a separate 'Malek Team' persona claimed a data leak; press reporting does not settle whether these are one operation [S10].
No 2024-2026 Pink Sandstorm operational reporting (for example during the 2025 Israel-Iran conflict) was found in the searches run.
The SentinelLabs confidence assessment is medium, and Check Point in 2023 called the affiliation not fully clear; no US government attribution was located [S4][S8].
The Unit 42 alias DEV-0022 and the Malpedia aliases DEV-0227 are not confirmed against Microsoft's current mapping [S2][S9].
Vendor profiles of UAE targeting were seen in search results but not verified from primary reporting, so the UAE is excluded from regions.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): Key terrain includes internet-facing web servers and VPN appliances, software vendors' update channels and database servers at Israeli and partner organizations [S5][S6][S7][S9]. The environment also includes the information space, where leak personas publish stolen data [S8]. STEP 2 (effects): Unpatched public-facing applications and trusted update paths let the actor turn one intrusion into many victims within hours [S6]. Ransomware branding hides state intent and complicates attribution and response priorities [S4]. STEP 3 (threat model): web-server exploit, then ASPXSpy web shell, then credential harvesting and lateral movement with public tools, then data theft (including Sqlextractor), then wiper or ransomware deployment and a leak via a persona [S7][S9]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is continued data theft followed by wiping or fake ransomware against Israeli education, technology and healthcare targets, amplified through hack-and-leak during periods of Israel-Iran tension [S9][S10]. MDCOA is a supply-chain wiper push through a trusted vendor, or a joint operation with Hezbollah-linked cyber actors such as Lebanese Cedar, hitting healthcare or partner-nation organizations at scale, including entities outside Israel [S6][S10]. Candidate indicators: ASPXSpy web shells on IIS servers; exploitation of known FortiOS or web-application CVEs; credential harvesting tools appearing weeks before a destructive event [S6]; new ransomware families with no payment infrastructure; and leak-persona claims after intrusions [S5][S7][S8].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: Track Israeli INCD and vendor reporting (Unit 42, Check Point, ESET), because the group's operations are usually first exposed through incident response [S6][S7][S9][S10]. Treat a 'ransomware' event at an Israel-linked or partner organization as possibly state-directed destruction [S4]. Authorities: The 'ransomware' framing can steer cases toward criminal channels. Coordinating early with intelligence and partner-nation cyber authorities supports a correct attribution and response posture [S4][S10]. Mission assurance: Prioritize patching internet-facing servers, monitoring for web shells, verifying the integrity of third-party software updates and maintaining offline backups for mission-relevant databases [S6][S7][S9]. Coordination: The INCD attributed the Ziv Medical Center attack to Agrius working with Hezbollah's Lebanese Cedar, so combined Iran-proxy activity needs coordination across CCMD and partner-nation boundaries, with information sharing with Israeli partners [S10].

provenance.importedSummary: Agrius is an Iranian threat actor active since 2020 notable for a series of ransomware and wiper operations in the Middle East, with an emphasis on Israeli targets. Public reporting has linked Agrius to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).
